headline: Dry, mild weather continues through Wednesday, a weak front arrives Thursday, and a possible weekend system is uncertain but will lower snow levels.
summary: As of Monday evening, forecasters expect quiet, dry weather across western Washington through Wednesday. A large area of low pressure offshore is sliding south toward California and will miss the region, while a weak ridge of high pressure to the north helps keep things calm. Patchy fog is possible over the next couple of mornings, mainly in cooler valleys, and some frost may form, especially in the south interior. High clouds should thin out late Tuesday, which should warm afternoons by a few degrees into Wednesday. The best chance of reaching 70 is in the south interior. A weak cold front passes Thursday into Friday, bringing cooler highs, more in the 50s. The best chance of rain or mountain precipitation is east of I-5 up to the Cascades. Some valleys and mountains may see 30s, with a few 20s possible. Another system may arrive next weekend, but computer models disagree on its path: some send it north into Canada, while others deepen it off the British Columbia coast. Whether rain or snow reaches the region is described as something of a tossup. Either way, snow levels (the elevation where precipitation changes from rain to snow) are expected to fall to 4,000 to 5,000 feet going into the weekend. Forecasters are fairly confident in the quiet pattern through Wednesday and more confident about the snow level drop than about the weekend rain details. No hazards are in effect.
changes: Earlier discussions focused on fog and put more emphasis on possible wind and rain Saturday into Sunday. By afternoon and evening, fog was described as limited, frost was added, and the weekend emphasis shifted to a tossup on precipitation with snow levels falling to 4,000 to 5,000 feet either way.
